description: Advanced regression family — LINEST, TREND, LOGEST, GROWTH, FREQUENCY (Excel 365). 35 perspectives (7 per function). Spill outputs flow through the same skip-oracle path as MUNIT and TEXTSPLIT (oracle compare_value cannot navigate ArrayValue). Live cases cover scalar error returns — LINEST/TREND/LOGEST/GROWTH share three error perspectives each (shape mismatch, singular system or y<=0, non-numeric cell); FREQUENCY surfaces error-cell propagation from data_array and bins_array. Tolerance widened to 1e-10 for stats-block fit metrics.

cases.skipped: LINEST stats=FALSE returns a 1x(k+1) spill of regression coefficients; oracle compare_value only handles scalars. Unit tests in linest_eval_test.cpp cover the slope/intercept content.

LINEST stats=TRUE returns a 5x(k+1) statistics matrix (coefficients, SEs, R^2, F, df_resid, ss_reg, ss_resid); oracle compare_value only handles scalars. Unit tests in linest_eval_test.cpp cover the full block.
LINEST multivariate (k>=2) returns a 1x(k+1) spill; oracle compare_value only handles scalars. Unit tests in linest_eval_test.cpp cover multivariate dispatch.
LINEST const=FALSE returns a spill with intercept slot=0; oracle compare_value only handles scalars. Unit tests in linest_eval_test.cpp cover intercept-suppression.
TREND with new_x omitted returns a column-vector spill of fitted y; oracle compare_value only handles scalars. Unit tests in trend_eval_test.cpp cover the default-new_x path.
TREND with explicit new_x returns a vector spill at the new observations; oracle compare_value only handles scalars. Unit tests in trend_eval_test.cpp cover the new_x path.
TREND multivariate returns a vector spill at the original observations; oracle compare_value only handles scalars. Unit tests in trend_eval_test.cpp cover multivariate prediction.
TREND const=FALSE forces fit through the origin and returns a vector spill; oracle compare_value only handles scalars. Unit tests in trend_eval_test.cpp cover intercept-suppression.
LOGEST stats=FALSE returns a 1x(k+1) spill of exp-coefficients; oracle compare_value only handles scalars. Unit tests in logest_growth_eval_test.cpp cover the m/b extraction.

LOGEST stats=TRUE returns a 5x(k+1) matrix (rows 2-5 stay on the linear log scale per Microsoft docs); oracle compare_value only handles scalars. Unit tests in logest_growth_eval_test.cpp cover the stats block.
LOGEST multivariate returns a 1x(k+1) spill of exp-coefficients; oracle compare_value only handles scalars. Unit tests in logest_growth_eval_test.cpp cover multivariate exp dispatch.
LOGEST const=FALSE puts exp(0)=1 in the intercept slot of the spill; oracle compare_value only handles scalars. Unit tests in logest_growth_eval_test.cpp cover the multiplicative-identity slot.
GROWTH with new_x omitted returns a column-vector exp-fit spill at known_x; oracle compare_value only handles scalars. Unit tests in logest_growth_eval_test.cpp cover the default-new_x path.
GROWTH with explicit new_x returns a vector spill at the new observations; oracle compare_value only handles scalars. Unit tests in logest_growth_eval_test.cpp cover the new_x path.
GROWTH multivariate returns a vector exp-fit spill; oracle compare_value only handles scalars. Unit tests in logest_growth_eval_test.cpp cover multivariate exp prediction.
GROWTH const=FALSE forces fit through y=1 and returns a vector spill; oracle compare_value only handles scalars. Unit tests in logest_growth_eval_test.cpp cover intercept-suppression.
FREQUENCY returns an (numeric_bins+1)x1 column spill of bucket counts; oracle compare_value only handles scalars. Unit tests in frequency_eval_test.cpp cover the basic distribution.
FREQUENCY with empty bins returns a 1x1 spill containing the count of numeric data; oracle compare_value only handles scalars. Unit tests in frequency_eval_test.cpp cover the degenerate-bins case.
FREQUENCY silently skips non-numeric data cells and returns a column spill; oracle compare_value only handles scalars. Unit tests in frequency_eval_test.cpp cover the skip-text path.

FREQUENCY does NOT sort bins internally; the output reflects the given bin order as a column spill; oracle compare_value only handles scalars. Unit tests in frequency_eval_test.cpp cover unsorted-bin order.

FREQUENCY routes data exceeding all bins into the trailing extra slot; the output is a column spill; oracle compare_value only handles scalars. Unit tests in frequency_eval_test.cpp cover the extra-slot fill.

FREQUENCY silently skips error cells in bins_array (matches Mac Excel) and returns a column spill; oracle compare_value only handles scalars. Unit test BuiltinsFrequency.ErrorInBinsArraySilentlySkipped covers the silent-skip semantics.
